brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases in a row at q=-1,0,0 (piece:-1,0,0;full), q=0,0,0 (piece:0,0,0;full) and q=1,0,0 (piece:1,0,0;full) — linear adjacent arrangement visible from above.
One bin per cell: bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain — all full-depth tray bins hanging on cell rims.

All three bins are hex-bin-full-drain variant with drain holes in floor; check_build meshClash clear. Bins filled with soil and planted (basil-young, mint-young, parsley-young) to show herb planter use.

finish.summary: Built 3-cell linear herb planter (-1,0,0 to 1,0,0) with three full-depth drained bins (hex-bin-full-drain), one per cell. Caps applied to open faces and joints locked. Each bin filled with soil and planted with herbs for demonstration — basil, mint and parsley — drains visible and verified.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
